channel.title: Home on arun._space
channel.description: Recent content in Home on arun._space

item.title: Whittle
item.description: An AI agent that lives on your Android phone and gets things done. Bring any model and your own keys, with no Whittle server in between.

item.title: Meh.ai
item.description: A Chrome extension for asking questions about the page you’re on, summarizing it and pulling out key points, with Gemini Nano running on-device. Built for the Google Chrome Built-in AI Challenge.

item.title: OpenVoice Streaming Server
item.description: A FastAPI WebSocket server that streams speech from the OpenVoice text-to-speech model.

item.title: 13 — Build a Mini-GPT
item.description: Every piece from lessons 1–12 assembled into a working character-level GPT in PyTorch — tokenisation, the full transformer stack, training loop, and text generation from scratch.

item.title: 12 — Pay Attention
item.description: Self-attention, Q/K/V, multi-head attention, positional encodings, and the transformer block — the mechanism behind every modern language model, explained from scratch.

item.title: 11 — The Machine That Remembers
item.description: Recurrent neural networks, hidden states, backprop through time, and why LSTMs were the memory upgrade that made sequences learnable.

item.title: 10 — Seeing with Filters
item.description: How convolutional neural networks see images — kernels, feature maps, pooling, and why a sliding 3×3 window beats a million fully-connected weights.

item.title: 09 — Too Good to Be True
item.description: When your network aces the training data and fails at everything else — overfitting, regularisation, dropout, and how to actually tell if your model is learning.

item.title: 08 — Just NumPy, No Magic
item.description: Stop using the concepts, start writing the code. A full neural network in pure Python and NumPy — same thing PyTorch does internally, just slower.

item.title: 07 — The Vanishing Act
item.description: Why deep networks went dark in the 90s — vanishing gradients, exploding gradients, and the tricks that finally made depth work: weight init, batch norm, and residual connections.

item.title: 06 — Watch It Learn
item.description: Forward pass, backprop, gradient descent — assembled into a training loop. Watch a network learn to separate XOR, circles, and spirals in real time.

item.title: 05 — Blame It on the Weights
item.description: Loss functions, gradient descent, and backpropagation — how a neural network looks at its mistakes and figures out exactly who to blame.

item.title: 04 — Dominos All the Way Down
item.description: The forward pass: how a number enters one end of a neural network and a prediction falls out the other, layer by layer.

item.title: 03 — The Switch That Isn't Really a Switch
item.description: Sigmoid, ReLU, tanh, softmax — the nonlinear magic that makes depth actually mean something.

item.title: 02 — Meet the World's Dumbest Brain Cell
item.description: One neuron. A handful of weights. A rule so simple it fits in one line. And yet — it learns. This is the perceptron, and it’s where everything begins.

item.title: 01 — The Numbers That Run Everything
item.description: Before we touch a single neuron, we need to speak its language. Vectors, matrices, derivatives, and the chain rule — the math that makes neural networks tick.

item.title: What If AI Understood Death? The Missing Piece of Survival Instinct
item.description: An exploration of how death awareness could transform AI from passive calculators into proactive partners with genuine survival instincts.

item.title: Beyond Words: Thought Communication
item.description: A visionary exploration of how humanity might transcend language, communicating thoughts, emotions, and concepts directly through new modalities.

item.title: Meh.ai
item.description: Discover how Meh.ai revolutionizes browsing by turning Chrome into your personal AI sidekick.

item.title: K-Armed Bandit Problem: From Casinos to Wall Street
item.description: An engaging exploration of the k-armed bandit problem, covering key concepts like exploration vs. exploitation, continuous rewards, and non-stationary environments.

item.title: OpenAPI to Function Calling: A Comprehensive Guide
item.description: Learn how to convert OpenAPI specs to AI-usable functions for smarter API interactions.

item.title: Defensive Distillation
item.description: An exploration of defensive distillation techniques to protect neural networks against adversarial attacks

item.title: About
item.description: I got my Master’s degree in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning from the Coimbatore Institute of Technology. Currently, I work as a Software Engineer – AI at Senseloaf.ai in Bengaluru, where I lead AI development for SIA, Senseloaf’s hiring platform. I build the AI across the hiring flow, from candidate matching and screening to a real-time voice interviewer, along with SIA’s agent harness, its MCP server, and internal tools for testing and monitoring agents.
